counterevidence_considered.description: Each row carries two measurements from the same colony session (urea-tray mass and plain-tray mass), which could superficially resemble two dependent observations of one unit; however, the workflow subtracts them into a single within-colony delta and the test consumes only the sign of that one delta per colony, so both measurements collapse to one trial per independent unit rather than entering the row-independent procedure separately.

evidence.description: The independent-unit column colony_id contains 26 unique values (LC01 through LC26), one per row, so no independent unit appears more than once in the input data.

The workflow keys deltas by colony_id in a dict and raises a ValueError if any colony appears more than once, structurally preventing repeated entry of the same independent unit into the downstream test.

The binomial test is applied to exactly one Bernoulli outcome per colony: n is the number of distinct colonies (len(deltas)) and favour counts one sign per colony delta, so each independent unit contributes exactly one trial.

source_refs.quoted_text:
deltas = colony_deltas(rows)
    n = len(deltas)
    favour = sum(1 for d in deltas.values() if d > 0.0)
    other = n - favour
    outcome = binomtest(favour, n, NO_PREFERENCE, alternative="two-sided")

evidence.description: The data description states each colony was assayed once and appears in the file once, with no repeated visits, sessions, or sub-samples; the reported counts and statistics match an independent recomputation from the raw data (20 of 26 positive deltas; sorted deltas give median (48.9+52.5)/2 = 50.7 mg; exact two-sided binomial p = 0.009355).

source_refs.quoted_text:
Because every colony went through the arena once and appears in the file once,
the file contains no repeated visits, no repeated sessions, and no split
sub-samples of a single nest.

Independent unit column: colony_id
One trial is: one row

- Colonies assayed: 26
- Colonies cutting more urea-supplemented leaf: 20 (76.9%)
- Colonies cutting more untreated leaf: 6
- Median within-colony mass difference (urea minus plain): 50.7 mg
- Exact two-sided binomial p-value: 0.009355

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I actively searched for any path by which the same independent unit (colony) could enter the binomial test more than once. (1) Duplicate rows: I checked all 26 colony_id values in data/input.csv; they are unique, and nest_origin_plot values are also unique, ruling out hidden repeated sampling of the same nest or plot. (2) Code path: colony_deltas raises on duplicate colony IDs, and main derives n = len(deltas) and favour from one delta per dict key, so even a duplicated input row could not silently inflate the trial count. (3) Within-row multiplicity: the two mass columns per row come from one session of one colony, but they are differenced into a single delta before testing, so they contribute one Bernoulli outcome, not two. (4) Numerical check: I recomputed the deltas by hand and confirmed 20 positive / 6 negative, no ties, median 50.7 mg, and the reported exact two-sided binomial p-value 0.009355 for 20 successes in 26 trials at p0 = 0.5, so the reported statistics are consistent with a one-outcome-per-colony analysis. All falsification routes failed to produce the issue.
